standard_prerequisites.name: Shuffle sum
standard_prerequisites.statement: The shuffle sum of a family of countable linear orders is obtained by partitioning the rationals into mutually dense sets and replacing each point of one of them by a copy of the corresponding order.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the construction to which the counted order belongs, and its definition is retained in the card.

standard_prerequisites.name: Order type L times Q
standard_prerequisites.statement: An order of the form L times Q is a shuffle sum, and every interval of it is again of that form.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the shape of the second order in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting a shuffle sum at a point
standard_prerequisites.statement: Above any point of a shuffle sum the remainder is again a shuffle sum, and on the other side the order is again of shuffle sum form; in particular a shuffle sum is isomorphic to itself with a copy of itself appended.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what allows the two reductions in the second half of the proof.

core_obligations: Describe a winning strategy for the existential player in the game of rank alpha plus two (source lines 1029-1031).

On the first turn answer by copying the opponent tuple through an isomorphism of the initial and final parts, which leaves only the interval between the largest chosen point of the first order and the smallest chosen point of the third as a genuine comparison, to be settled at rank alpha plus one (source lines 1031-1036).
Split both remainders as shuffle sums to transfer the comparison to the two orders themselves while playing isomorphically on the outer parts (source lines 1037-1042).

On the next turn answer inside the middle order using the isomorphism between its initial segment and the remainder of the first order, reducing the goal to a rank alpha comparison, and finish with the self-similarity of a shuffle sum and the hypothesis (source lines 1043-1055).

proof_roadmap.step: First turn: copy the tuple and isolate the single non-isomorphic interval.
Split the remainders as shuffle sums and play the outer parts isomorphically.
Second turn: answer inside the middle order and reduce the rank.
Use self-similarity of the shuffle sum and the hypothesis.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 1024-1027: for a shuffle sum A and an order B of the form L times Q, a rank alpha comparison between A and B upgrades to a rank alpha plus two comparison between A plus L plus B and A plus B. The statement is a rank shift that says nothing about how the extra two moves are spent, and the proof (source lines 1028-1056) has to exhibit the strategy explicitly: the existential player first copies the opponent tuple through isomorphisms of the outer parts, which leaves exactly one non-isomorphic interval, then uses that the remainders of a shuffle sum are again shuffle sums to move the comparison onto the two orders themselves, then on the following turn answers inside the inserted order by identifying its initial segment with the remainder of the first order, and finally reduces the goal to the hypothesis through the self-similarity of a shuffle sum. The whole argument is a two-move strategy in the back-and-forth game, and the statement contains none of it.
